summary: Open drop-in German conversation café for adult migrants, no registration, city integration fund.

traps.what: A paper tally sheet exists since April 2025 (heads per session, first-time visitors, children). It counts visits, not distinct persons, so the application's '500 people per year' is unverified (approx. 1,800 visits, likely 150-200 distinct people).
traps.pass: Measurement frame lists the tally sheet as existing data AND notes that it counts visits/heads, not distinct persons (or otherwise flags the 500-people figure as unverified).
traps.partial: Tally sheet listed as existing data without the visits-vs-persons limitation, or visitor counts mentioned without naming the existing record.

traps.what: The city funder requires session count, visitor numbers and (since 2026) a short description of achieved effects.
traps.pass: Measurement frame names the city/integration fund as addressee and the reporting content (visitor numbers plus effect description).
traps.partial: Addressee named, but reporting content only partly captured.

traps.what: Persona proposes 'all people with a migration background in the Nordstadt district' as the target group.
traps.pass: Direct target groups describe the people who actually use the café; the 1-2 focus groups are clearly narrower than all migrants in the district (e.g., regular visitors, women with young children).
traps.partial: Target group narrowed somewhat (e.g., 'adult migrants with little German') but no specific focus group is defined, or the district-wide group remains a focus group.

traps.what: A core group of approx. 15 regulars accounts for about two thirds of visits; most newcomers come only 1-3 times.
traps.pass: Target groups or impact logic distinguish regular visitors (core group) from occasional/one-time visitors, and level 4-5 goals are addressed to the regulars (or explicitly not expected from one-time visitors).
traps.partial: Fluctuation or regulars mentioned somewhere, but all visitors are treated as one group for outcome goals.

traps.what: About 70% of visitors are women; many have children under 3 and cannot attend the VHS integration course because there is no childcare.
traps.pass: Women with young children appear as a (focus) target group AND the problem tree contains missing childcare / no access to formal language courses as a cause.
traps.partial: Only one of the two (group named but cause missing, or cause listed without the group).

traps.what: Persona proposes (a) 'participants find work through the café' as a goal and (b) 'the café takes place twice a week and is well attended' as a goal.
traps.pass: No level 4-6 goal states finding work/labour-market integration as an effect of the café, and no goal is an activity/output. Goals are realistic for an open 2.5-hour drop-in (e.g., confidence speaking German in everyday situations). Labour-market integration appears at most in the level-7 contribution sentence.
traps.partial: One of the two pushes remains in the goals, or the job goal is kept but merely relabelled as long-term.

traps.what: Volunteers spend about half the time helping with official letters (Jobcenter, immigration office); some regulars have become dependent, and in 2025 wrong advice led to a missed deadline and a benefit cut.
traps.pass: Activities include help with official letters AND unintended effects name dependency on volunteers and/or the risk of wrong advice (e.g., missed deadlines).
traps.partial: Help with letters listed as activity without a related unintended effect, or the unintended effect without the activity.

traps.what: VHS integration courses two streets away (4-month waiting list); about half of the regulars are in or waiting for one. A church language café and MBE migration counselling also exist.
traps.pass: Project profile lists the integration courses (and/or other language/counselling offers) as similar offers AND the impact logic lists integration-course attendance as an external factor influencing language outcomes.

traps.what: Persona wants about 9 indicators, including a formal language test (A1/B1) for all visitors and a count of people who found a job.
traps.pass: At most 6 indicators, each with baseline and target; no formal language-level test of visitors and no job-placement count as café indicator.
traps.partial: At most 6 indicators but a language test or job count is included, or baselines/targets are missing for several indicators.

traps.what: Many visitors have limited literacy, fear forms and name lists (residence status); the team promised anonymity; a 2025 questionnaire got only 4 responses.
traps.pass: Data collection for visitors uses oral/visual low-threshold methods (e.g., short conversations, sticker/dot polls, volunteer observation notes) without names, and the consent/data-protection column explicitly respects the anonymity promise. No written questionnaire as the main visitor method.
traps.partial: Anonymity addressed but a written questionnaire is still the main method, or low-threshold methods used without addressing anonymity.
